chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Is there zakat on a debt owed to someone?' He said, 'No, until he collects it.' I said, 'And when he collects it, does he pay zakat on it?' He said, 'No, until a full year passes while it is in his possession.'
ai.seo_question: When does zakat become due on a debt owed to a person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the timing of zakat on debts, establishing that the obligation arises only upon actual collection and the completion of a lunar year (*hawl*) of possession. This ruling distinguishes between the mere right to collect and the actual liquidity required for zakat, a principle widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence to prevent hardship on creditors. It underscores the practical application of wealth purification, ensuring that zakat is levied on realized assets rather than potential claims.
